body.p:
Real-Chief was making a canoe. It was a travelling canoe which Real-Chief / made. He had with him his child, K·iōʼł. / A big hat was there upside down on the ground. / The big hat lay upside down at the place where Real-Chief was making the canoe. Then his child was playing on the ground, He tried to forbid his child / to go near the big hat / which was lying on the ground upside down. It was the hat of Screecher-of-the-Sky [Thunderbird]. He went near it and some thing happened.
He put the hat on and / then the hat flew away with K·iōʼł, [the child] / of Real-Chief. He was taken to the house of the Thunderbird. / Real-Chief cried on account of his lost child. "O, my K·iōʼł," thus Real-Chief said while he was crying / on account of K·iōʼł.

Then he went home / to his house. Again he went away, crying everywhere. Then / big mucus hung out of his nose on account of his crying. Then / he made up his mind that he would make a child out of his mucus. He blew his nose and put the mucus into a mussel shell. / That was the place into which he put his mucus, Then it became a person. / It grew up and the mussel shell became too small. / Then he changed it and put it into a clam shell. / It grew a little and [this shell] became too small. Then he changed it again / and put it into the shell of a large mussel. / Again it grew and he changed it again. Again he put it into another one, / into the shell of a horse clam. / Then it became a big man. Now he had it for a son. He carried him in his arms. / He was crying, the Mucus-Boy was crying all the time. Then he became tired / on account of the crying of Mucus-Boy. He became angry and threw him down, / "He keeps on crying all the time, this bad Mucus-Boy." / Then the one who tried to be his child lay as a puddle on the floor.

Then [Real-Chief] went about crying again. / He tried to bring back his child K·iōʼł. / "Oh, if you would come back to me, my K·iōʼł!" / K·iōʼł tried to come to him. "Now I have come back. I have returned. / I am your K·iōʼł. Do not cry." - "You are the only one who does not come to make fun of me. / My K·iōʼł was not thus on the side of his face." / Thus he said. Then he was just left by his K·iōʼł. His K·iōʼł flew away. Then
it was as if he was stretching down his legs / and the tattooing, on the legs of his K·iōʼł was seen. / Then he tried again to shout after him. He gave it up / and K·iōʼł just did not come back.

Then he went home again. Real-Chief thought / he would revenge himself on him / who had made disappear his son. In the morning he arose / and went to hire Pitch. "I come to hire you, / Pitch," said Real-Chief. Then the mother of Pitch did not want to let him go, / "Else you will melt," said his mother. Then he went to another place to / Frost to hire him, and his mother also would not let him go, / "Else he will melt at once."- I, am going to cover him with a mat, " / said Real-Chief. "Well, go, my dear," said his mother. He went. He arrived, / and Real-Chief stepped out of the canoe. Then he was working. / Then he made a whale. Then the sun arose. / He shouted at him, "Pitch!" said he. He answered and shouted, "Ho," said he. / Thus said Pitch, and Frost also said, "Ho!". Thus also said Frost. Then Real-Chief was working again. / He thought of / his companions and he shouted again to Pitch, and he said again / "Ho!". Then his voice did not sound right. Then / the sun rose higher. Frost!" - "Ho!" he said again. Then the voice of Frost did not sound right. Now / the men whom he had hired were melting. He went to work again. Then he shouted / again, "Pitch!" he said again "Ho!" Pitch almost / [did not] answer because he was melting. / "Frost!" Real-Chief also said, and Frost almost did not answer. / Behold, they were nearly entirely melted. He went to work again
/ at the work he was doing. Then he shouted again, "Pitch!" / said he again. "Ho! Pitch almost [did not] answer: / "Frost:" he also said, / but he did not answer. They melted when it was noon. / Behold, they were melted / and therefore they did not answer. Now they lay / in the bottom of his canoe. It was covered with water / and on top was the pitch that had melted. Behold, he had hired them for putting pitch on the whale he was making. Behold, he was working / and Real-Chief finished the whale he was making. / He had become pitch and for this reason he had hired him, in order to put pitch on / the whale he was making. It was finished and / his younger brothers went into it. They ‘launched it. They tried it and the big one blew, the whale made by Roal-Chief. / Then he hired Muskrat to dig up the whale he had made whenever it stuck in the mud. / Four times it blew. Then saw. / Screecher-of-the-Sky what Real-Chief had planned to take revenge. He sent / his youngest child, "Go, One-Whale-Carrier, and grasp that little whale," he said / to his youngest child. One-Whale-Carrier went. / The whale came up and blew, and One-Whale-Carrier grasped it. / He almost lifted it, but / he was not strong enough. "Run to the fore end, younger brothers," said Real-Chief to his younger brothers. / Then the whale made by Real Chief went down / and just stuck in the mud with its big face. / Muskrat began to dig. Then it came off / and blew again. Then Screecher-of-the-Sky sent Two-Whale-Carrier. He also went. The whale blew again and / Two-Whale-Carrier grasped it. Then he raised it a little higher, but could
/ not. He was not strong enough and stuck / to the pitch on the whale made by / Real-Chief. It went down again / and stuck in the mud. Muskrat began to dig again. / "Muskrat, dig it out," thus Muskrat was told. Then / it came up again and blew again. / Now was sent Three-Whale-Carrier to go and grasp / what his younger brothers had tried to get. He went / and the whale blow again. Three-Whale-Carrier grasped it. He raised it higher than the rest had, much higher. / "Run to the fore end, younger brothers;" / said Real-Chief to his / younger brothers, speaking wisely. / They ran to the fore end. Again the wings [of the bird] stuck [to the whale]. It went again and went down in the water / and a gain it stuck to the bottom. / Muskrat was told again to dig it out / "Dig away, Muskrat, dig away, Muskrat," he was told again. / Then Muskrat dug it out and it came up again. It blew again and Screecher-of-the-Sky again told his eldest / son, "Go, Four-Whale-Carrier, truly it must be / a great body that destroyed your brothers." / Four-Whale-Carrier went. The whale blew. Four-Whale-Carrier grasped it. / He went up. "Run to the fore end, younger brothers. We made a mistake, younger brothers," said he when he / became frightened and when they were going up. / [Four-Whale-Carrier] almost carried them to the door of the house of / Screecher-of-the-Sky. Then his wings stuck to the pitch of the whale made by Real-Chief. / He went and came down. He came down to the water and [the whale] stuck / to the ground. [Muskrat] began to dig again. Then Real-Chief had tried to kill all / the children of Screecher-of-the-Sky. / That is the end.
